episodes.174724: An upper level trough which moved through the region on December 3 and 4 brought another round of widespread precipitation to the area. This system picked up some warm tropical moisture which resulted in snow levels being rather high for much of the duration of this event. While significant snowfall did fall above 8000 feet, moderate to locally heavy rainfall below the snow line as much of the Sierra Nevada picked up between 2 and 4 inches of rainfall while the adjacent foothills picked up between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain and the San Joaquin Valley picked up between half an inch and an inch of rainfall. A rockslide was reported near Mariposa which resulted in some brief road closures. Much like with the December 1 and 2 storm, amounts were much lower in Kern County where most stations only picked up a tenth of an inch or less of rainfall.
episodes.176477: A surge of subtropical moisture moved into the region during the 3rd as a result of southwest flow that developed from an upper-level low located along the west coast and an upper-level high pressure along the Gulf coast states. As a result of this moisture surge, precipitable water values rose to between 1.2-1.4 inches across most of central and southern Arizona, resulting in an extended period of light to moderate rain. Waves of rain affected central and southern Arizona from the morning of the 3rd through the early morning hours of 4th. Most of the Phoenix metro area received upwards of an inch while the areas towards the south, into Pinal County, as well as across the higher terrain towards the east received upwards of 2-3 inches. Even though most of the area did not see flooding from this rainfall event, due to the light rainfall rates, elevated flow along several washes in northwestern Pinal County lead to areal flooding, mainly across Arizona City, where there were reports of intersections flooded with stalled cars.

events.narrative: California Highway Patrol reported rocks in the roadway at the intersection of Ben Hur Road and Silver Bar Road.

Images from the Pinal County Sheriff Office indicated several low water crossings around Arizona City flooded, resulting in multiple disabled vehicles. Due to the prolonged period of flooding, some school districts around the area closed down the following day. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in the area. The most likely reason for the flooding was the washes that run through the area likely overflowed. No injuries were reported.
